name: New York
title: Family holidays in New York
intro: Huge parks, rooftop views and a pretzel on every corner. Here's what New York is like with the family, when to go and how long to stay.
facts_note: Check entry rules on GOV.UK before you book.
when_to_go: Spring and early autumn are mild and good for walking all day. Summer is hot and busy, but school holidays make it the easy choice for many families. December is cold, crowded and very festive.

things.name: Central Park
things.blurb: Rowing boats, playgrounds and plenty of space to let off steam.

things.name: American Museum of Natural History
things.blurb: Dinosaur halls and a life-size blue whale. Go early on a weekday.

things.name: Staten Island Ferry
things.blurb: A free crossing with views of the Statue of Liberty and the skyline.

things.name: The High Line
things.blurb: A park built on an old railway line, raised above the West Side.

things.name: Top of the Rock
things.blurb: An open-air deck with the Empire State Building in full view.

things.name: Coney Island
things.blurb: Beach, boardwalk and fairground rides at the end of the subway line.

faqs.question: Is New York good for a family holiday?
faqs.answer: Yes, if your family enjoys walking and busy streets. The parks, museums and ferries suit all ages, and the subway makes it easy to get around without a car.

faqs.question: How many nights do you need?
faqs.answer: Four to six nights covers the big sights at a family pace. The first day often goes on jet lag, so plan something light.

faqs.question: Do UK families need a visa?
faqs.answer: Most British passport holders, children included, apply for an ESTA online before they fly rather than a visa. Check GOV.UK for the current rules.

faqs.question: When is New York cheapest?
faqs.answer: January to early March, outside school holidays. It's cold, but flights and hotels usually cost less.
